# dataversecontact_custom_api (Resource)

Manages a custom API configuration in the Dataverse Contact API. The schema is saved as a draft and immediately published. `tiers` decides which of /{public,me,team,all}/actions/{name} it answers on, and `target` / `callerParameters` how a call is checked — see the Custom APIs guide.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Registers a Dataverse Custom API as an invokable route. The schema is the
# CustomApiHint JSON — inline via jsonencode, or file("....customapi.json").
resource "dataversecontact_custom_api" "expand_calendar" {
  scope      = "default"
  route_name = "expand-calendar"

  schema_json = jsonencode({
    routeName              = "expand-calendar"
    dataverseUniqueName    = "ExpandCalendar"
    requiredPermission     = "expand-calendar:invoke"
    isFunction             = true # GET (function) rather than POST (action)
    publicInvoke           = true # callable without authentication
    bindingType            = "entity"
    boundEntityLogicalName = "calendar"
    boundEntitySetName     = "calendars"
    requestParameters = [
      { uniqueName = "Start", type = "datetime" },
      { uniqueName = "End", type = "datetime" },
    ]
  })
}

# A custom API acting on the caller's own case: answers on
# /me/actions/close-incident/{caseId} and /team/actions/close-incident/{caseId}.
# The case id in the URL is checked against the "case" route's scoping and
# written into IncidentResolution.incidentid@odata.bind. Needs the API release
# with tiered custom APIs.
resource "dataversecontact_custom_api" "close_incident" {
  scope      = "default"
  route_name = "close-incident"

  schema_json = jsonencode({
    routeName           = "close-incident"
    dataverseUniqueName = "CloseIncident"
    isFunction          = false
    bindingType         = "global"
    tiers               = ["me", "team"]
    target = {
      table        = "case"
      recordIdPath = "IncidentResolution.incidentid@odata.bind"
      filters      = ["statecode eq 0"]
    }
    requestParameters = [
      { uniqueName = "IncidentResolution", type = "entity" },
      { uniqueName = "Status", type = "integer" },
    ]
  })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `route_name` (String) The URL-friendly route name for this custom API.
- `schema_json` (String) The custom API schema as a JSON string (CustomApiHint format: routeName, dataverseUniqueName, displayName, description, requiredPermission (optional, defaults to {routeName}:invoke), isFunction, bindingType, boundEntitySetName, tiers, target, callerParameters, requestParameters, responseProperties; the legacy publicInvoke and ownershipCheck are still accepted — see the Custom APIs guide for the shapes and the rules the API enforces on apply). Usually jsonencode(...) or file("....customapi.json").
- `scope` (String) The scope this custom API belongs to.

### Read-Only

- `binding_type` (String) The binding type ("global", "entity", "entityCollection").
- `dataverse_unique_name` (String) The Dataverse unique name for this custom API.
- `id` (String) Resource identifier in the format {scope}/{route_name}.
- `is_function` (Boolean) Whether this is a function (GET) or action (POST).
- `source` (String) The source of the published schema ("published", "built-in").

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import id is {scope}/{route_name}
terraform import dataversecontact_custom_api.expand_calendar default/expand-calendar
```
